topics.reference_answer: Lifecycle assessment (LCA) of lithium-ion batteries addresses three themes: (1) Material recovery: Three recycling routes exist — pyrometallurgical (smelting, low selectivity), hydrometallurgical (acid leaching, 90%+ Li/Co/Ni recovery, most mature), and direct recycling (relithiation, preserves cathode structure, lowest energy). Recovery rates of Co (>95%), Li (80-95%), Ni (>90%) vary by route. (2) Environmental impact: Manufacturing accounts for 40-60% of lifetime GHG emissions; recycling reduces cradle-to-gate impact by 30-50% vs primary production; carbon footprint varies by energy mix (fossil vs renewable). Battery chemistry matters: LFP lower cobalt impact vs NMC. (3) Battery supply chain: Critical material concentration (Li: Chile/Australia, Co: DRC) creates geopolitical risk; EU Battery Regulation mandates recycled content and digital battery passports; second-life reuse before recycling can extend value chain.
